unit.title: CSS: boxes and spacing
unit.description: width and height, padding, border, margin, block and inline elements, centering a box

cards.definition: Set the size of the content area of an element, for example 300px wide and 200px tall.
cards.example: .card { width: 300px; } keeps every card 300 pixels wide.

cards.definition: The space INSIDE a box, between its content and its border; it shows the background color of the box.
cards.example: button { padding: 12px 24px; } gives the label room to breathe.

cards.definition: The space OUTSIDE a box, between its border and the elements around it; it is always transparent.
cards.example: p { margin-bottom: 16px; } leaves a gap under each paragraph.

cards.definition: The line drawn around a box, between padding and margin. The shorthand gives width, style and color: 2px solid black.
cards.example: .card { border: 1px solid #ddd; } draws a thin light gray frame.

cards.definition: Block elements (div, p, h1) start on a new line and take the full width; inline ones (span, a, strong) sit inside a line of text.
cards.example: Two <span> stay side by side; two <div> stack one under the other.

cards.definition: margin: 0 auto on a block that has a set width puts equal automatic space on its left and right.
cards.example: .page { width: 800px; margin: 0 auto; } centers the page column.

exercises.prompt: Which property sets the space INSIDE a box, between the text and the border?
exercises.explain: padding is the inside space (it shows the background color). margin is the outside space (always transparent).
whyWrong: margin is the space OUTSIDE the border.
border is the line itself, not a space.
spacing is not a CSS property.

exercises.prompt: Which property pushes a box away from the elements around it?
exercises.explain: margin adds transparent space outside the border, pushing the neighbors away.
whyWrong: padding adds space inside the box, between content and border.
width sets the size of the content, not the space around it.
outline draws a line around the box without taking any space.

exercises.prompt: Put the layers of a box in order, from the inside out.
exercises.explain: Content first, then padding (inside space), then the border line, then margin (outside space).

exercises.prompt: How wide is this box, from one border to the other?
exercises.explain: By default, padding and border are added to the width: 100 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 1 = 122px.
whyWrong: 100px is only the content: padding and border are added on each side.
Padding and border count twice: once on the left, once on the right.
You added the padding on both sides but forgot the border.

exercises.prompt: What does border: 2px solid red; draw?
choices: A solid red line, 2px thick, around the box
A red background, 2px from the edge
exercises.explain: The border shorthand gives the width (2px), the style (solid) and the color (red) in one line.
whyWrong: border draws a line; the background is set with background-color.
solid means a continuous line; a dashed one is written dashed.
Text color and shadows have their own properties.

exercises.prompt: Which of these elements is INLINE: it stays inside a line of text?
exercises.explain: Inline elements (span, a, strong) flow inside a line. Block elements (div, p, h1) stack and take the full width.
whyWrong: <div> is a block: it starts on a new line.
is a block: each paragraph starts on a new line.
<h1> is a block: headings take the full width.

exercises.prompt: By default, a <div> placed after another <div> appears on a new line, below it.
exercises.explain: div is a block element: blocks stack vertically and take all the width available.

exercises.prompt: This box has a set width. What goes in place of "___" to center it on the page?
exercises.explain: margin: 0 auto means no space above and below, and equal automatic space left and right: the block is centered.
whyWrong: text-align centers the text INSIDE the box, not the box itself.
padding cannot be set to auto.
align is not a CSS property.

exercises.prompt: Build a declaration that adds 16 pixels of space inside a box, on every side.
exercises.explain: padding: 16px; adds space inside the box, on all four sides.

exercises.prompt: The card should have a thin gray border, but none appears. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: A border needs a style to be visible: border: 1px solid gray; Without solid (or dashed, dotted), the style stays none.

choices: 10px top and bottom, 20px left and right
10px left and right, 20px top and bottom
10px at the top, 20px at the bottom
exercises.explain: With two values, the first one is for top and bottom, the second one for left and right.
whyWrong: The first value is vertical (top and bottom), the second horizontal.
Two values mean vertical then horizontal, not top then bottom.
Each side gets one of the two values, not both.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that gives every .card a thin solid gray border.
exercises.explain: .card { border: 1px solid gray; } The border shorthand gives a width, a style and a color.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that centers .page horizontally (it already has a width).
exercises.explain: .page { margin: 0 auto; } No space above and below, equal automatic space left and right.
